memberdef.definition: typedef void(* XUartLite_Handler)(void *CallBackRef, unsigned int ByteCount)
memberdef.name: XUartLite_Handler

briefdescription.para: Defines the callback function type for send and receive operations.

detaileddescription.para: The first argument is a callback reference passed in by the upper layer when setting the callback functions, and passed back to the upper layer when the callback is invoked. The second argument is the ByteCount which is the number of bytes that actually moved from/to the buffer provided in the _Send/_Receive call.

The receive and transmit FIFOs of the UART are not flushed, so they may be flushed if desired. The hardware device does not have any way to disable the receiver such that any valid data may be present in the receive FIFO. This function disables the UART interrupt. The baudrate and format of the data are fixed in the hardware at hardware build time.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if everything starts up as expected.
XST_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND if the device is not found in the configuration table.

simplesect.para: In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.

briefdescription.para: Looks up the device configuration based on the unique device ID or base address.

detaileddescription.para: The XUartLite_ConfigTable[] contains the configuration info for each device in the system.

simplesect.para: A pointer to the configuration found or NULL if the specified device ID/BaseAddress was not found. See xuartlite.h for the definition of XUartLite_Config.
In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.

detaileddescription.para: The receive and transmit FIFOs of the UART are not flushed, so you may want to flush them. The hardware device does not have any way to disable the receiver such that any valid data may be present in the receive FIFO. This function disables the UART interrupt. The baudrate and format of the data are fixed in the hardware at hardware build time.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to a structure containing information about a specific UART Lite device. This function initializes an InstancePtr object for a specific device specified by the contents of Config. This function can initialize multiple instance objects with the use of multiple calls giving different Config information on each call.

Device base address in the virtual memory address space. The caller is responsible for keeping the address mapping from EffectiveAddr to the device physical base address unchanged once this function is invoked. Unexpected errors may occur if the address mapping changes after this function is called. If address translation is not used, use Config->BaseAddress for this parameters, passing the physical address instead.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if everything starts up as expected.

simplesect.para: The Config pointer argument is not used by this function, but is provided to keep the function signature consistent with other drivers.

briefdescription.para: Resets the FIFOs, both transmit and receive, of the UART.

detaileddescription.para: The FIFOs are emptied. Since the UART does not have any way to disable it from receiving data, it may be necessary for the application to reset the FIFOs to get rid of any unwanted data.

briefdescription.para: Sends the specified buffer of data using the UART.

detaileddescription.para: This function operates in either polled or interrupt driven modes. It is non-blocking such that it returns before the data has been sent by the UART. If the UART is busy sending data, it returns and indicates zero bytes were sent.
In a polled mode, this function only sends as much data as the UART can buffer in the FIFO. The application may need to call it repeatedly to send a buffer.

In interrupt mode, this function starts sending the specified buffer and then the interrupt handler of the driver continues sending data until the buffer has been sent. A callback function, as specified by the application, is called to indicate the completion of sending the buffer.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a buffer of data to send.
Number of bytes to send. A value of zero stops a previous send operation that is in progress in interrupt mode. Any data that was already put into the transmit FIFO is sent.

simplesect.para: The number of bytes actually sent.
The number of bytes is not asserted so that this function may be called with a value of zero to stop an operation that is already in progress.

briefdescription.para: Receives a specified number of bytes of data from the UART.

detaileddescription.para: This function attempts to receive the data and store it into the specified buffer. It is designed for either polled or interrupt driven modes. It is non-blocking such that it returns if no data has already been received by the UART.

In a polled mode, this function only receives as much data as the UART can buffer in the FIFO. The application may need to call it repeatedly to receive a buffer. Polled mode is the default mode of operation for the driver.

In interrupt mode, this function starts receiving and then the interrupt handler of the driver continues receiving data until the buffer has been received. A callback function, as specified by the application, is called to indicate the completion of receiving the buffer or when any receive errors or timeouts occur.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to buffer to receive data into.
Number of bytes to receive. A value of zero stops a previous receive operation that is in progress in interrupt mode.

simplesect.para: The number of bytes is not asserted so that this function may be called with a value of zero to stop an operation that is already in progress.

briefdescription.para: Determines if the specified UART is sending data.

detaileddescription.para: If the transmitter register is not empty, it is sending data.

simplesect.para: A value of TRUE if the UART is sending data, otherwise FALSE.

briefdescription.para: Returns a snapshot of the current statistics in the structure specified.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a XUartLiteStats structure to where the statistics are to be copied.

briefdescription.para: Zeros the statistics for the given instance.
Runs a self-test on the device hardware.

detaileddescription.para: Since there is no way to perform a loopback in the hardware, this test can only check the state of the status register to verify it is correct. This test assumes that the hardware device is still in its reset state, but has been initialized with the Initialize function.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the self-test was successful.
XST_FAILURE if the self-test failed, the status register value was not correct.

detaileddescription.para: An interrupt occurs when data is received or data has been transmitted. The device contains 16 byte receive and transmit FIFOs such that an interrupt is generated anytime there is data in the receive FIFO and when the transmit FIFO transitions from not empty to empty.
After calling this function, data may still be received by the UART but no interrupt is generated since the hardware device has no way to disable the receiver.
This function sets the handler called when an event (interrupt) occurs in the driver. The handler allows application-specific processing.

parameterdescription.para: Upper layer callback reference passed back when the callback function is invoked.

simplesect.para: There is no assert on the CallBackRef since the driver does not know what it is (nor should it)

briefdescription.para: Handles interrupts for the UART Lite driver.

detaileddescription.para: It must be connected to an interrupt system such that it is called when an interrupt for any UART lite occurs. This function does not save or restore the processor context such that the caller must ensure this occurs.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the instance of the UART that the interrupt is for.
